title: Παῖς λουόμενος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 297. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Παῖς ποτε λουόμενος ἔν τινι ποταμῷ ἐκινδύνευσεν ἀποπνιγῆναι.
sentences.tr: Pais pote louomenos en tini potamōi ekindyneusen apopnigēnai.
sentences.l: A boy once, bathing in a certain river, was in danger of drowning.
sentences.n: κινδυνεύω with the infinitive is 'run the risk of doing'. ἀποπνίγομαι is to be choked off — of water, to drown.

sentences.t: Ἰδὼν δέ τινα ὁδοιπόρον, τοῦτον ἐπὶ βοηθείᾳ ἐκάλει.
sentences.tr: Idōn de tina hodoiporon, touton epi boētheiāi ekalei.
sentences.l: And having seen a certain traveller, he kept calling on him for help.
sentences.n: ἐπί with the dative gives the purpose a thing is done for: 'with a view to help'. ἐκάλει is imperfect, and the calling goes on while the danger does.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ ἐμέμφετο τῷ παιδὶ ὡς τολμηρῷ.
sentences.tr: Ho de emempheto tōi paidi hōs tolmērōi.
sentences.l: But he found fault with the boy as being reckless.
sentences.n: μέμφομαι takes the dative of the person blamed. ὡς with the dative adjective gives the ground of the blame as the blamer sees it — he faulted him on the score of recklessness.

sentences.t: Τὸ δὲ μειράκιον εἶπε πρὸς αὐτόν· « Ἀλλὰ νῦν μοι βοήθει, ὕστερον δὲ σωθέντι μέμψῃ. »
sentences.tr: To de meirakion eipe pros auton· « Alla nyn moi boēthei, hysteron de sōthenti mempsēi. »
sentences.l: But the lad said to him: « Well, help me now; afterwards, once I have been saved, you shall blame me. »
sentences.n: μειράκιον, a lad or stripling, replaces παῖς here; the Greek shifts the word, not the boy. σωθέντι is a dative aorist passive participle agreeing with the μοι carried over from the first clause: 'blame me once I have been saved'. μέμψῃ is future middle, second singular — a plain future doing the work of a concession, 'then you may blame me all you like'.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος εἴρηται πρὸς τοὺς ἀφορμὴν καθ’ ἑαυτῶν διδόντας ἀδικεῖσθαι.
sentences.tr: Ho logos eirētai pros tous aphormēn kath’ heautōn didontas adikeisthai.
sentences.l: The story has been spoken against those who give occasion against themselves to be wronged.
sentences.i: The story is aimed at those who themselves furnish the grounds for the wrong they suffer.
sentences.n: εἴρηται is the perfect passive belonging to λέγω, 'has been spoken'; πρός with the accusative here is 'directed against'. ἀφορμή is the starting-point a thing can be taken from, and so the handle or occasion; κατά with the genitive is 'against'. The same closing formula, with a different charge after it, stands at fable 77.
